description: Top-level ownership and dependency manifest for SwissKnife source modules.

classificationValues.browser-safe: May be statically imported by browser bundles.
classificationValues.host-only: May use Node, process, filesystem, terminal, subprocess, native, or server-only APIs and must not be statically imported by browser bundles.
classificationValues.host-ui: Terminal or Ink UI that runs on the host and must not be treated as browser UI.
classificationValues.split: Contains both browser-safe and host-only code; browser imports must use documented browser-safe entrypoints only.
classificationValues.universal: Runtime-neutral types, constants, and pure helpers.
classificationValues.unknown: Not classified; new imports require review before use.

rules: Imports should point to the same layer or an earlier layer in dependencyDirection unless the importing module is an explicit composition layer.
Browser entrypoints may import only modules or entrypoints classified as browser-safe or universal.
Host-only modules may import split modules only through host-safe or environment-neutral entrypoints.
shared and utils must not become owners of domain behavior; domain-specific helpers belong in the owning module.
New public imports should be added to publicEntrypoints before other modules depend on them.

__mocks__.purpose: Test doubles and module mocks for unit and integration tests.
notes: Mocks are not production runtime modules.

auth.purpose: API key, delegation, DID keystore, and UCAN authentication helpers.
auth.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe auth adapters
notes: Host credentials and filesystem-backed key stores must stay behind host entrypoints.

cli.purpose: Legacy CLI parser and registry compatibility code.
notes: New process roots belong in src/entrypoints and command behavior belongs in src/commands.

client.purpose: Protocol clients used by host and integration surfaces.
client.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe client adapters
notes: Clients that use Node transports are host-only.

cloudflare.purpose: Cloudflare worker deployment and runtime integration helpers.
notes: Deployment clients are host-only; worker templates must remain browser/worker-safe.

config.purpose: Configuration initialization, schemas, migration, and persistence orchestration.
config.browserReachability: allowed only for pure schemas and browser-safe config readers
notes: Filesystem-backed configuration is host-only.

connectors.purpose: External connector adapters and data lake integration surfaces.
connectors.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe or remote connector adapters
notes: Connector credentials and host SDKs must not be statically imported by browser code.

constants.purpose: Product constants, prompts, model constants, release note constants, and static terminal assets.
notes: Constants should stay data-only and avoid runtime dependencies.

core.purpose: Core execution primitives that predate the current module split.
notes: New code should prefer a more specific owning module.

documentation.purpose: Documentation generation and repository documentation automation.
notes: Documentation generation may use filesystem and process APIs.

graph.purpose: Graph and IPLD graph helpers not yet moved into storage or inference.
graph.browserReachability: allowed only for pure graph helpers
notes: Persistence-backed graph behavior should move to storage or inference.

huggingface.purpose: Hugging Face service adapters and Cloudflare worker integrations.
huggingface.browserReachability: allowed only for browser-safe remote adapters
notes: Provider SDK and credential handling is host-only unless explicitly browser-safe.

integration.purpose: Cross-module integration bridges, registries, and initialization glue.
notes: Integration modules compose owned runtime modules but should not become new domain owners.

ipfs.purpose: IPFS client and IPFS runtime adapters outside the storage module.
ipfs.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe IPFS clients
notes: IPFS persistence code should converge with src/storage/ipfs over time.

lib.purpose: Legacy library helpers and collaboration code not yet assigned to narrower modules.
notes: New domain behavior should move to a named owning module instead of lib.

ml.purpose: Machine learning tensor, optimizer, hardware, and inference support code.
ml.browserReachability: allowed only for browser-safe ML adapters and pure tensor helpers
notes: Native acceleration and hardware probing are host-only unless isolated by adapter.

patches.browserReachability: forbidden unless an individual patch is documented as browser-safe
notes: Patches should be explicit and temporary.

platform.purpose: Explicit browser and host platform facades for runtime-specific capabilities.
notes: src/platform/browser.ts must remain browser-safe and must not import host modules.
src/platform/host.ts is the Node process, filesystem, subprocess, CLI, MCP, and command loading boundary.

performance.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe measurement APIs
notes: Host profiling and process metrics must stay out of browser bundles.
Release helpers may use filesystem, process, and package-manager APIs.
Testing helpers are not production runtime dependencies.

tools.purpose: Interactive tool implementations and tool support types.
tools.browserReachability: forbidden unless exposed through a remote/tool protocol boundary
notes: Host tools may use filesystem and process APIs; browser access should go through tool descriptors or remote execution.

types.browserReachability: allowed for type-only and runtime-neutral exports
notes: New cross-runtime contracts should move to src/shared/types.

ux.purpose: User-experience helpers outside the terminal component hierarchy.
notes: Browser UX should live under web/ or a future browser UI module.

vector.purpose: Vector search, embedding, and vector storage helpers.
vector.browserReachability: allowed only for browser-safe vector adapters
notes: Vector persistence should use storage boundaries.

commands.purpose: CLI command definitions, command handlers, help generation, and command-specific orchestration.
notes: Command modules may render terminal UI and may use process, filesystem, and network clients.
Browser adapters must call commands through a protocol boundary, never by static import.

entrypoints.purpose: Executable process roots and top-level runtime bootstrapping.
notes: Entrypoints are composition roots and may import host-only modules.
Browser application roots live under web/ and must not import src/entrypoints.

components.purpose: Reusable Ink terminal UI components and message renderers.
notes: These components are host terminal UI, not browser UI.
Browser React components live under the separately owned src/components/browser module.
Command-specific presentation should stay here only when reusable across commands or screens.

components-browser.purpose: Browser-safe React components that render inside web and browser runtime surfaces.
notes: Browser UI must use browser-safe hooks and platform facades instead of terminal Ink components.
Host-only CLI presentation remains under src/components.

screens.purpose: Whole-screen Ink flows that compose components, hooks, and command state.
notes: Screens may import command types but should not invoke command handlers directly.
Browser screens live under the separately owned src/screens/browser module.

screens-browser.purpose: Browser-safe full-screen React flows for web and browser runtime surfaces.
notes: Browser screens may compose only browser-safe components, hooks, platform facades, shared contracts, and utilities.
Terminal Ink screen flows remain under src/screens.

hooks.purpose: React and Ink hooks for terminal interaction, permissions, logging, and input state.
hooks.browserReachability: forbidden unless a hook is explicitly documented as browser-safe
notes: Existing hooks read terminal streams and process state, so the directory is host UI by default.
Browser-safe hooks live under the separately owned src/hooks/browser module.

hooks-browser.purpose: Browser-safe React hooks for web and browser runtime surfaces.
notes: Browser hooks must depend on browser platform facades and universal contracts.
Terminal Ink hooks remain under src/hooks.

service-apps.purpose: Application manifests, generated app state, capability policy contracts, all-tools app bindings, and release policy gates.
service-apps.browserReachability: allowed through app manifest and capability contract modules
notes: App-visible capability policy and manifest shape belongs here; protocol mechanics stay in src/services/mcp.

service-bridge.purpose: Typed modal/prover bridge adapters that sit below the root service facades.
service-bridge.browserReachability: allowed only through explicitly browser-safe bridge contracts
notes: Bridge implementation files are owned here instead of by the root service inventory.

service-deontic.purpose: Deontic extraction, graph, legal norm, parser quality, and support-map services.
service-deontic.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe parser and contract entrypoints
notes: Root deontic compatibility files remain explicitly inventoried under audit.serviceRootFileOwners.

service-fol.purpose: First-order logic conversion, export, formatting, and confidence scoring services.
service-fol.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe conversion and formatting contracts
notes: FOL domain implementation files belong here; root FOL facades are inventoried separately.

service-fol-utils.purpose: FOL parser/output utility entrypoints shared by root FOL service facades.
service-fol-utils.browserReachability: allowed only through audited parser/formatter contracts
notes: This is a service-owned utility family, not generic src/utils ownership.

service-glasses.purpose: Meta glasses display, input, webapp, mobile ORB, and hardware-free replay adapters.
service-glasses.browserReachability: allowed through display, widget, and mobile ORB browser-safe adapters
notes: Display/orb adapters and glasses-specific fallbacks belong here; app policy source data stays in src/services/apps.

service-integrations.purpose: External runtime integrations that are isolated from root compatibility files.
service-integrations.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe integration adapters
notes: New external integration files must land here or in a new named service family.

service-ipfs.purpose: IPFS MCP/UI descriptors, descriptor packs, ORB profiles, proof-cache integration, and browser/host IPFS service adapters.
service-ipfs.browserReachability: allowed through browser-safe descriptor and transport modules
notes: IPFS descriptors and storage integration live here; generic IPFS clients remain under src/ipfs and storage persistence under src/storage/ipfs.

service-logic.purpose: Logic calculus, bridge, parser, proof, and policy service implementations migrated under the logic service family.
service-logic.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe logic service entrypoints
notes: Fine-grained logic-family ownership remains documented in src/services/module-ownership.json.

service-mcp.purpose: MCP/MCP++ protocol, transport, ORB routing, UI profile contracts, mediation, registry, and generated IDL descriptor logic.
service-mcp.browserReachability: allowed through browser-safe protocol and transport modules
notes: Protocol, transport, mediation, and ORB machinery belongs here; descriptor packs for IPFS-owned apps stay in src/services/ipfs.

service-platform.purpose: Platform service adapters migrated out of the root services namespace.
service-platform.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe platform service adapters
notes: Runtime-wide platform facades remain under src/platform; service-specific platform adapters live here.

service-proof-engine.purpose: Proof execution, routing, cache, and explanation services.
service-proof-engine.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe proof-engine entrypoints
notes: Root proof-engine compatibility files remain in the explicit root service inventory.

service-provers.purpose: Browser and host prover bridges, serializers, proof-cache helpers, and prover type contracts.
service-provers.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe prover contracts and WASM/browser adapters
notes: Root prover compatibility files remain in the explicit root service inventory.

service-shared.purpose: Pure cross-service helpers that are shared by service-family modules without owning runtime state.
notes: Generic application-wide shared contracts remain under src/shared.

service-zkp.purpose: ZKP browser backends, simulated prover quarantine, UCAN bridge, artifacts, and circuits.
service-zkp.browserReachability: allowed only through audited browser-safe ZKP backend entrypoints
notes: ZKP artifacts and circuits are service-owned data/code assets and must not be duplicated at src/services root.

services.purpose: Explicitly inventoried root service facades and compatibility files. New service implementation files must live in a named service family subdirectory.
services.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe service files or explicitly classified neutral files
notes: Root-level service source files are compatibility/root facades only and must be listed in audit.serviceRootFileOwners.
New service implementation files must land under a named service family such as src/services/mcp, src/services/ipfs, src/services/provers, or src/services/zkp.
Browser-safe service files must be listed in audit.browserSafeServiceFiles before browser-facing code imports them.
Host adapters must be isolated by filename or submodule before they are imported from browser-facing code.

storage.purpose: Storage providers, registries, virtual filesystem abstractions, cache backends, and IPFS storage integration.
storage.browserReachability: allowed only through browser-safe providers and interfaces
notes: Filesystem-backed storage is host-only.
Browser storage must use a browser-specific provider and may not import filesystem backends.
Browser imports should use src/storage/browser.ts, which selects between IndexedDB, OPFS, Cache Storage, or an injected IPFS transport and never imports Node fs, path, or process.
Host imports that need Node filesystem, path, or process/config-driven storage should use src/storage/host.ts.

tasks.purpose: Task graph, decomposition, delegation, scheduling, synthesis, and coordination primitives.
tasks.browserReachability: allowed for pure graph and scheduler primitives; managers that invoke AI or host workers require review
notes: Pure graph and scheduler code should remain runtime-neutral.
Execution that needs worker threads, subprocesses, or model SDKs belongs behind host-only adapters.

workers.purpose: Worker pool management, worker-thread execution, and task execution isolation.
workers.browserReachability: src/workers/browser.ts is browser-safe; every Node worker_threads, filesystem, and subprocess worker entrypoint is host-only
notes: Browser imports must use src/workers/browser.ts, which is built only on Web Worker APIs (Worker/SharedWorker, postMessage, transferable objects) and never imports worker_threads, child_process, fs, or path.
Host imports that need node:worker_threads, node:child_process (subprocess workers), or filesystem-based worker script resolution should use src/workers/host.ts.

src/workers/pool.ts, thread.ts, worker.ts, worker-pool.ts, worker-thread.ts, pool/worker-pool.ts, and execution/worker-script.js are private, host-only legacy Node worker_threads implementations; src/workers/host.ts re-exports the supported subset (worker-pool.ts + worker-thread.ts) and adds a node:child_process subprocess worker runtime.
build-tools/configs/vite.workers.config.ts builds only src/workers/browser.ts; it must never gain a Node worker_threads/child_process/fs/path entry point.

The static scripts in public/workers/*.js are already browser-safe Web Worker scripts loaded only by URL (new Worker(url)); src/workers/browser.ts references them by path via BROWSER_WORKER_SCRIPTS instead of importing them.

ai.purpose: AI service facade, agents, model abstractions, thinking graphs, and AI tool execution.
ai.browserReachability: allowed only through fetch-based or environment-neutral adapters
notes: Browser imports should use src/ai/browser.ts; host imports that need config, process.env, provider SDKs, terminal tools, or task integration should use src/ai/host.ts.
Provider SDKs and process.env access are host-only unless wrapped by a browser-safe remote or fetch adapter.
AI code should depend on model interfaces rather than command or UI modules.

models.purpose: Model registry, provider metadata, model initialization, and model execution services.
models.browserReachability: allowed for provider metadata and pure registry code; execution code requires adapter review
notes: Browser imports should use src/models/browser.ts for pure provider metadata and fetch-compatible adapters.
Host imports that need config, process.env, bridge execution, local files, subprocesses, provider SDKs, or native runtimes should use src/models/host.ts.
Model execution that reads process.env or uses host SDKs must stay out of browser bundles.

inference.purpose: Higher-level inference engines such as graph RAG, swarm inference, and WebNN serving surfaces.
inference.browserReachability: allowed only for browser-native inference adapters and pure data structures
notes: Browser inference must use browser-native APIs, WASM, or remote adapters explicitly marked browser-safe.
Server-style inference endpoints remain host-only.

shared.purpose: Cross-runtime contracts, constants, events, types, and small pure helpers that are intentionally shared.
notes: shared is the lowest layer and must remain domain-neutral.
If a helper needs runtime state, IO, or a domain dependency, it belongs outside shared.

utils.purpose: Small reusable utilities for formatting, config access, logging, terminal handling, browser helpers, errors, and low-level adapters.
utils.browserReachability: allowed only for browser-safe files such as src/utils/browser.ts and pure helpers
notes: Utilities do not own product behavior.
Host-only utilities must stay out of browser bundles unless accessed through a runtime boundary.
